points.description: States that the appetitive faculty corresponds to Plato's theory of the soul (tripartite soul), explicitly naming Plato.
points.partial_credit: Only 'three parts/divisions of the soul' stated without naming Plato earns 0.5.

points.description: States that the appetitive faculty is the part of the soul dealing with desires and passions (appetites), and that it is one of the three divisions of the soul.
points.partial_credit: Gives desires/passions but omits that it is one of the three divisions of the soul: 0.5.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both: naming Plato's theory of the soul (three-part soul) and stating that the appetitive part deals with desires and passions as one of three divisions. Vague answers such as 'the mind' or 'human behaviour' earn nothing. A wrong attribution (e.g. Aristotle, Freud) or describing it as reason or spirit/courage loses that point.
